Under this workspace's own rule that is a ramp item and not a capability cap, so it does not drag the score below the pass line; but scoring it 10 would hide the single question most likely to be asked, and his own QA has already tagged that question `screening`. Alongside it sit two thinner absences a Chief-Architect round can reach: no ANN-internals evidence (no HNSW parameters, no quantisation, no dimensionality) and no vector corpus scale figure.

8.5 / 10 — the strongest criterion on this seat, and still not a 10.

What earns the 8.5: KQ1 is not a RAG demo, it is a production retrieval service he solely owned from design through rollout, and the design decisions are the ones a Principal Architect is hired to make. Decision-not-Patient as the retrieval unit. Filters as contracts rather than weights, with the reason stated ("a soft weight would let a very similar protocol-B decision leak into a protocol-A result") and the second-order consequence named (empty-result rate and NDCG stay separately measurable). Tenant filter inside the kNN query rather than applied after it. Embeddings cached by content hash plus model version. Cache keys pinning the index manifest so a blue-green index swap makes stale entries unreachable instead of merely expired. A shadow-evaluated index build that fails closed onto yesterday's index and pages the on-call. A cold-start gate that refuses to answer on thin data. Per-program recall floors because averages hide weak segments. Most candidates for this seat will describe a Pinecone integration; he can describe an index lifecycle, a correctness-first cache, and an eval contract.

What holds it below 9.5: semantic query routing is one of four architecture bullets this JD names in exactly this area, and he has no instance of it. The brief's guess — that KQ10 candidate-proposal is the nearest thing — is wrong on the evidence: KQ10's finders fan out concurrently to every domain and are then re-verified at a barrier, which is fan-out, not routing. The two genuine analogues are KQ1's persona-1 parse of clinician free text into a typed QueryCase (NL query understanding, no retrieval) and KQ10's pre-hoc easy/hard classifier routing to an 8B or 70B tier with a post-hoc confidence escalation. He should lead with those two, in that order, and say plainly that he architected query understanding and cost-tier routing but has not built an index-or-tool router — then design one out loud, because with ten services each carrying its own index he has the most natural substrate for that answer anyone will hear that day.

Two things to fix before this goes anywhere near a room. First, the word "hybrid": his means filters plus dense, the market's often means BM25 plus dense with RRF, and one qualifying clause closes a gap that otherwise reads as a hole. Second, and more urgent — his own journey doc still rehearses "a retrieval pipeline over Amazon Neptune". The résumé was corrected; the spoken script was not. On a retrieval seat that is the first question asked, and he is currently rehearsed to answer it with the wrong store.
